## Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities

## Business Continuity Plan during the 6 th Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization

Hong Kong will host the 6 th Ministerial  Conference  of  the  World  Trade  Organization  (MC6) from 13 th to  18 th December 2005 at the Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wanchai.  Over 10,000 international delegates, participants and journalists are expected to attend the event. As a result, there are associated risks that must be managed carefully.

Judging from past experiences in other jurisdictions, there is a possibility that demonstrations may take place in Hong Kong around the time of the MC6.  These activities may range from peaceful  demonstrations  to  more  forceful  incidents  such  as  damage  to  property  and  business premises, traffic disruption and closing access to affected areas.  In addition, there is also the danger of possible disruption to Internet trading and other online financial services.  All these potential events may interrupt your firm's operations.

In particular, the Police will establish a security cordon around the Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wanchai, being the venue for the said conference, from Tamar east to the Wanchai ferry pier and south as far as Harbour Road. Businesses located within the security cordon may be significantly disrupted. In addition, the implementation of this and other security measures may disturb transport services.

Consequently, all licensed corporations and associated entities, in particular those with offices or operations in Wanchai or Admiralty areas, are reminded to:

- (i) implement an effective business continuity plan ('BCP') appropriate to their scale of business and business responsibilities (note 1);
- (ii) ensure adequate measures are in place to protect their physical security and that of their  mission-critical computer networks and internet services; and
- (iii) in light of the potential security issues as well as possible traffic or road closures, we are  encouraging  firms  to  carefully  consider  the  logistical  aspects  of  any  important new business initiatives, major system enhancements or operational changes that they may want to undertake before and during the MC6 period.

Intermediaries Supervision Department Intermediaries and Investment Products Division Securities and Futures Commission

Note  1:  Please  refer  to  paragraph  36  in  the  Appendix  to  the  Management,  Supervision  and  Internal Control Guidelines for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (April 2003)
